The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 db9f0de04f757cf3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 40. statement: There are finite alphabets A1, . . . , AJ, depending only on Y, k and the fixed constants, and online random maps ξt : Y −→ A1 × · · · × AJ with the following properties. Each coordinate cell at level j has diameter at most 40rj and an anchor within 20rj of all its points. Thus ξt is injective. Give the full alphabet tree the leaf distance rj−1 when the first differing coordinate is j. For the selected hidden members X1 t , . . . , Xk t , P := E ∑ t k ∑ a=1 dT ( ξt−1(Xa t−1), ξt(Xa t ) ) ≤ CℓQ + Dpart. (7.2) Here C is absolute and Dpart < ∞ is independent of the input law and its horizon. A coordinate label common to successive maps has a fixed anchor, except for the explicit heavy-ball reuse below, when its anchor moves by at most 40rj.
